content:
Starting today, WhatsApp Web users can view, review, and annotate PDF files without leaving the conversation. Here are the details.

Adobe Acrobat has landed on WhatsApp Web

Previously, when receiving PDF files on WhatsApp, users had to download the file before opening it, and there were no built-in tools for reviewing or annotating documents.

Adobe announced today (yesterday) that its Acrobat PDF tools have been directly integrated into WhatsApp Web and the Windows version of the WhatsApp application, allowing users to open, review, and annotate documents without downloading files or leaving conversations.

The company stated that in addition to standard PDF files, this integration also supports password-protected documents, and files shared in conversations continue to be protected by WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption, "meaning only members of the conversation can read its content," according to Adobe.

Adobe noted that this integration reflects the growing number of users using WhatsApp on larger screens to handle tasks such as reviewing contracts, invoices, forms, and assignments, and also embodies its broader strategy of bringing Acrobat's PDF tools to the platforms where users work daily, such as Chrome, Microsoft 365 and Copilot, ChatGPT, Workday, and so on.
